title: DFI ASL600 Packages Low-Power Intel Compute Into a SMARC 2.2 Module
seoTitle: DFI ASL600 Brings Low-Power Edge AI to SMARC 2.2
socialTitle: DFI ASL600 Brings Low-Power Edge AI to SMARC 2.2
seoDescription: DFI’s ASL600 packages low-power industrial edge computing into an 82 × 50 mm SMARC 2.2 module with MIPI-CSI, dual 2.5GbE and CAN.
dek: DFI’s ASL600 uses the 82 × 50 mm SMARC 2.2 form factor with low-power Intel processors, MIPI-CSI, dual 2.5GbE and wide-temperature support for compact edge systems.
summary: ASL600 is less about peak AI throughput than preserving a product’s carrier-board investment while giving compact vision, HMI and robot-controller designs a standardized compute module.
whyItMatters: The standardized SMARC form factor separates the compute module from the carrier board, helping OEMs preserve I/O and mechanical work across processor changes.
MIPI-CSI, dual 2.5GbE and dual CAN make the module relevant to vision, HMI and compact robot-control designs.
A -40°C to 85°C operating range and fanless orientation target harsh embedded deployments rather than consumer notebooks.

reporting.heading: SMARC shifts the redesign boundary
paragraphs: Instead of integrating the processor directly onto a custom motherboard, the ASL600 packages Intel Atom x7000RE, Processor N or Core 3 N options on an 82 × 50 mm SMARC 2.2 module.
This lets an OEM invest in a carrier board for product-specific I/O while keeping a more replaceable compute core, which can be useful for long-lived industrial products.

reporting.heading: The I/O mix is unusually relevant to compact vision systems
paragraphs: DFI routes MIPI-CSI, dual Intel I226 2.5GbE, dual CAN and multiple display interfaces through the module. That combination maps well to compact machine-vision, HMI and AGV/AMR controller designs.
The value is not high-end NPU performance; it is integration density, low-power operation and a standardized upgrade path.

reporting.heading: Thermal and lifecycle claims need SKU-level validation
paragraphs: DFI highlights fanless use and operation from -40°C to 85°C, but final thermal behaviour depends on processor SKU, enclosure and sustained workload.
For design-in, buyers still need module pricing, carrier availability, exact AI capability by CPU option and the support horizon of the selected configuration.

flypigTake: ASL600 is attractive when mechanical stability and carrier-board reuse matter more than peak AI TOPS. FlyPig would position it as a compact embedded-compute route that can pair with external accelerators if the application later needs more inference performance.
productStatus: DFI has published the ASL600 module and its core SMARC 2.2 specifications, including industrial temperature claims. Processor variant, carrier and software support determine production readiness.
openQuestions: Which processor, memory and software configurations are available with long-term supply commitments?
Which carrier boards, camera modules and environmental validations are offered for evaluation?
canadaRelevance: Canadian industrial, transportation and compact-robotics teams may value a replaceable SMARC module with camera and industrial networking when power and enclosure space are constrained.
